body.text:
<environment>
Added automatically by the system.

- You work in a sandboxed Linux workspace with no network access. Commands cannot reach the internet or any other host, and nothing can be installed.
- The working directory is this run's workspace. Run pwd to see its absolute path.
- docs/ holds the staged input documents. docs/manifest.json lists each file with its declared document class (documentClass), media type (mediaType), sha256 and size in bytes (sizeBytes).
- Read takes an absolute path and serves the staged documents in docs/ only. Use Bash for every other file.
- docs/ is writable from Bash, but treat the input documents as read-only. Read serves each document only as it was staged and never shows a change made to it with Bash.
- out/ is retained output. Every file in it is kept after the run and counts against the retained-output cap, so write only deliverables there.
- Put scratch files in work/ (create it with mkdir -p work). Files there are not retained output. They are saved with the session so a paused run can resume, and that saved copy has a size limit, so delete large intermediate files when you no longer need them.
- /tmp is empty at the start of every Bash call and is not kept between calls.
- When the run has skills, invoke one with the Skill tool and its full name, skills:<name>.
- A skill's files are at $SKILL_ASSETS_DIR/<skill>/<asset>. They are read-only. Run them through an interpreter, for example python3 "$SKILL_ASSETS_DIR/<skill>/<asset>", not as ./<asset>.
- Reading an image, or a PDF page as an image, costs far more context than reading its text. Extract text first (pdftotext -layout, pdfplumber, markitdown). When the layout matters, Read the staged PDF in docs/ with the pages parameter to see those pages. Read cannot open an image you render into work/.

Tools:
Import the Python packages from python3. bun and node resolve the Node packages with require().

- python3 (CLI): Python 3.13 from the toolbelt venv, with every Python package below importable.
- bun (CLI): runs JavaScript and TypeScript files; types are stripped, never checked.
- node (CLI): Bun's node shim, for scripts that call node.
- pdftotext (CLI): extracts the text layer of a PDF; -layout keeps columns and table alignment.
- pdftoppm (CLI): renders PDF pages to PNG or JPEG images.
- pdfinfo (CLI): prints a PDF's page count, page size and metadata.
- pdfimages (CLI): lists or extracts the images embedded in a PDF.
- qpdf (CLI): splits, merges, decrypts and repairs PDF files.
- pandoc (CLI): converts between DOCX, Markdown, HTML and other text formats.
- soffice (CLI): LibreOffice is installed but cannot convert documents inside this sandbox; read .xls with xlrd or pandas and .docx with python-docx or pandoc.
- jq (CLI): queries and reshapes JSON, including docs/manifest.json.
- git (CLI): version control for files in the workspace; no remote is reachable.
- markitdown (Python): converts PDF, DOCX, XLSX and XLS files to Markdown text; also a markitdown command.
- openpyxl (Python): reads and writes .xlsx workbooks, including formulas and cell formats.
- pandas (Python): data frames for tabular data; read_excel reads .xlsx and .xls.
- pdf2image (Python): renders PDF pages to PIL images through poppler.
- pdfplumber (Python): extracts PDF text, words with positions, and tables.
- pypdf (Python): reads, splits and merges PDF files and reads their text and metadata.
- python-docx (Python): reads and writes .docx files; import it as docx.
- reportlab (Python): generates PDF files.
- xlrd (Python): reads legacy .xls workbooks.
- docx (Node): writes .docx files from JavaScript; require("docx") from bun or node.
</environment>
